quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign show?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right when both arrive at the same time, whether the intersection is controlled by signs or signals or uncontrolled.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
You may only proceed if a circular green light is also showing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. However, you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You see a flashing red traffic light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, give other drivers the right-of-way, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. What happens?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver may go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, if you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink, possess, or have open alcohol containers in a vehicle on any public road. This applies to all passengers and locations in the vehicle.

questions.question: Another driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane is available, slowly reduce your speed when the road ahead is clear to let them pass.

questions.explanation: If tailgated, move right if possible. If not, slowly reduce speed when safe to encourage them to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: How long must a driver practice on a probationary license?
questions.explanation: A driver must practice unsupervised driving for at least one year on a probationary license before getting a basic driver license. During this time, follow all restrictions on your probationary license.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. This yellow and black sign warns of bicycles crossing the road.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly that they appear drunk. Coffee, open windows, and loud radio are not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert to road dangers.

questions.question: A transit bus is signaling to re-enter the main road after stopping. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit bus that signals to enter the main road after loading or unloading passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using sirens or air horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when the way is clearly safe.

questions.question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted across traffic lanes?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where they must stop.

questions.question: Another car is about to hit you. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if another driver appears about to hit you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is using its siren and/or flashing lights. What must you do immediately?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights, sirens, or other warning devices, immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes as another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must you show the officer?
questions.explanation: You must provide your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. You are required to have all three documents in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: Where should you grip the steering wheel during normal driving?
questions.explanation: Think of your steering wheel as a clock face. Hold it on both sides at the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock positions. Keep your thumbs along the rim of the wheel.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, what should you know?

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians are responsible to stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where they can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What happens if you break the rules on a Graduated Driver License?

options.text: Will result only in points against the driver's license.
Will result in no negative consequences.
May result in a fine and license suspension.

questions.correctAnswerText: May result in a fine and license suspension.
questions.explanation: New drivers must follow all Graduated Driver License rules. Breaking these rules may result in a $100 fine and suspension of your license.

questions.question: What is a good rule to follow when passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so that you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers to your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass, there is a greater chance of a crash. Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic and within the legal speed limit. Only pass when you need to.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look around, and move forward carefully.

questions.question: What should a worried, nervous, angry, or crying driver do?

options.text: Will drive no differently than they would if they were thinking more clearly.
Can drive faster because they are more in touch with their senses.
Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to vent while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving. Calm down and focus before you start the engine.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing train tracks. Obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with motor vehicles and bicyclists.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
You need to make sure there is space for your vehicle to get all the way across the tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to make sure there is space for your vehicle to get all the way across the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough room to cross completely before entering the tracks. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: When do roads freeze quickly?
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, shaded areas under trees or buildings freeze faster than other parts of the road. These areas are also the last to dry.

questions.question: On a slippery road, what should a driver with Anti-Lock Brakes do if the car loses traction?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal hard and hold it steady, then steer away from danger. The ABS system will pump the brakes automatically, faster than you can. Releasing pressure or pumping the brakes yourself will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the crossing guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the rules that would apply if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a crossing guard, sign, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow what the traffic light shows.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic lights. The only exception is when a police officer is directing traffic instead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left and then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about hazards ahead. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves right and then left.

questions.question: You can practice driving with a valid learner permit:
questions.explanation: With a valid learner permit, you cannot drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles with sirens, air horns, or flashing red, blue, or white lights go first. Pull over to the right side of the road when you can. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have lost control of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: You should use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which of the following traffic signals?
questions.explanation: A solid green arrow means you can drive in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: You should leave more space than usual when stopping:
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you have room to avoid a crash.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a curve in the road ahead.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, what should a driver do?

options.text: Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where they can see at least 200 feet on both sides, even if they enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where they can see approaching traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where they can see approaching traffic clearly before entering the intersecting roadway.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic. Do not enter the intersecting roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What lights must you use when driving in rain?
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When other drivers go around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger signaling, or a train's warning sound. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after coming to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows laws you must obey. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. What headlight setting should you use?

options.text: High or low beam. Either is fine.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another vehicle. Switch to low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Give your body time to remove the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time to remove the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change your BAC or how alcohol affects you.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before using the brakes.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. Release the accelerator first to let your vehicle slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly. This activates your brake lights and helps prevent rear-end collisions.
